title: Venus: Earth’s Evil Twin
objective: After this level you can compare Venus and Earth and describe Venus’s surface and odd rotation.
summary: Venus matches Earth’s size but has 90 times the air pressure, acid clouds, and spins backwards so slowly its day outlasts its year.

cards.headline: On Venus, a day is longer than a year.
A twin gone wrong
cards.body: Venus is nearly the same size as Earth. There the resemblance ends: the air pressure at its surface is about 90 times Earth’s, and the planet is wrapped in thick clouds of sulfuric acid.

cards.headline: Backwards and slow
cards.body: Venus spins backwards compared with most planets, so the Sun rises in the west. It spins so slowly that one rotation takes 243 Earth days, longer than its 225-day trip around the Sun.

cards.fact: The Soviet Venera landers reached Venus’s surface.
cards.context: In the 1970s and 1980s they sent back the first pictures from the ground, then were destroyed by the heat and pressure within about two hours.

cards.headline: Venus: surveyed
learned: It spins backwards: the Sun rises in the west
Its day (243 days) outlasts its year (225)

questions.prompt: What are Venus’s clouds made of?

options.label: Frozen carbon dioxide crystals
options.rationale: Its atmosphere is carbon dioxide, but the clouds are acid.

questions.explanation: Venus is covered by thick clouds of sulfuric acid.

questions.prompt: Why is a day on Venus longer than its year?

options.label: Venus orbits the Sun unusually fast
options.rationale: Its 225-day year is ordinary; its spin is the odd part.

options.label: Venus has no day and night at all
options.rationale: It does, just very long ones.

options.label: It rotates so slowly that one spin takes longer than one orbit
Its thick clouds block all sunlight
options.rationale: Clouds don’t change the length of a day.

questions.explanation: Venus takes 243 Earth days to rotate once but only 225 to orbit the Sun, so its rotation outlasts its year.

questions.prompt: From Level 11: on Earth the Sun rises in the east because Earth spins west to east. What does a western sunrise on Venus tell you?

options.label: Venus spins the opposite way to Earth
Venus orbits the Sun backwards
options.rationale: It orbits the same way as the other planets.

options.label: Venus has no axis to spin around

questions.explanation: A sunrise in the west means Venus rotates backwards compared with Earth and most planets.
